title: Billy Sims: 1978 Heisman Winner Who Built a BBQ Brand
question: What year did Billy Sims win the Heisman and what did he do after football?
answer: Billy Sims won the 1978 Heisman Trophy as a junior after leading the nation with 1,762 rushing yards. After his NFL career he co-founded Billy Sims Barbecue, which opened its first restaurant in Tulsa in 2004.
summary: Billy Sims won the 1978 Heisman with a nation-best 1,762 rushing yards, went No. 1 in the NFL draft and later co-founded the Billy Sims Barbecue chain.
body: Billy Sims took a winding road to Norman. Born in St. Louis, he moved to Hooks, Texas, as an eighth grader to live with his grandmother, and he joined Oklahoma as a freshman on the 1975 national championship team. An injury early in 1976 earned him an extra year of eligibility, and by 1978 he was ready to take over.

That junior season was spectacular. Sims ran for 1,762 yards at 7.6 yards per carry and scored 20 rushing touchdowns, leading the country in rushing and setting a Big Eight single-season record. The Heisman vote was one of the more unusual ones: Penn State's Chuck Fusina actually received more first-place votes, 163 to 151, but Sims won the trophy on total points, 827 to 750. He ran for 1,506 yards in 1979 and finished second to USC's Charles White.

The Detroit Lions made him the first overall pick in 1980, and he responded with 1,303 rushing yards and Rookie of the Year honors. He made the Pro Bowl in each of his first three seasons before a knee injury in 1984 ended his career.

Sims found a lasting second act in food. In 2004 he and Jeff Jackson opened the first Billy Sims Barbecue in Tulsa's Farm Shopping Center, and the company now describes itself as a 30-plus unit brand operating in six states, with Sims still active in the business, visiting locations and greeting fans. He entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 1995.
